newsitem.title: UK: Thai plans ex-London cargo fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Thai plans ex-London cargo fuel surcharge.

text.p: Thai Airways International Ltd is planning an ex-London cargo fuel surcharge in line with the six pence per kg announced by British Airways Plc on October 31, Thai UK cargo manager, Mike Miller said.

He told Reuters in a telephone interview that the airline's Bangkok head office had said any move to introduce a surcharge should depend, "on the decision taken by the local national carrier and the outcome of the International Air Transport Association(IATA) meeting on November 13."
Since BA has said it will apply a six pence cargo surcharge on intecontinental routes from November 8, "I'm proposing to follow them subject to head office agreement," Miller added.
The British carrier is applying a smaller surcharge of three pence a kg for freight on European and domestic routes.

The emergency IATA meeting has been called to discuss the impact of the sharp rise of jet-fuel prices in the last few months on both passenger and cargo operations, industry sources said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
